Ampere runs that OpenClaw environment for you, so you do not need to manage servers, updates, uptime, or setup. 🦞OpenClawThe open-source assistant engine.AmpereThe hosted product that runs OpenClaw for you. Why use Ampere? Use Ampere when you want an assistant that stays available, works from your channels, and can grow with your workflows. Ampere helps with: hosted OpenClaw setup dashboard chat and saved sessions Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and other channel setup skills and scheduled jobs workspace files and terminal access billing, credits, updates, and support The short version: OpenClaw is the assistant. Ampere runs it. title: Media Generation
description: Choose image generation and image edit defaults
content: AdvancedMedia GenerationChoose image generation and image edit defaultsMedia Generation settings control which visual models Ampere uses for image work. Ampere separates two defaults: Image Generation — create a new image from a prompt Image Edit — edit or improve an existing image This lets you use one model for first drafts and another for refinements. When to change these settings Change media settings if you: create images often want more control over cost and quality want different defaults for creating and editing do repeated visual work and do not want to choose a model each time If you rarely create images, the defaults are fine. How to use it Open Media Generation settingsGo to the dashboard settings area.Pick an Image Generation modelChoose the default model for new images.Pick an Image Edit modelChoose the default model for refinements.Save your choicesAmpere uses these defaults for future image tasks. Current media models The current product UI includes: GPT Image 1.5 (gpt-image-1.5) Seedream 4.5 (seedream-4.5) Nano Banana Pro (nano-banana-pro) Nano Banana 2 (nano-banana-2) Flux 2 Flex (flux-2-flex) Standard vs HD Each model shows a Standard and HD credit cost. ⚡StandardLower cost. Best for drafts, prompt testing, and quick variations.💎HDHigher cost. Best for final images and polished outputs. Simple workflow: test in Standard, finish in HD. title: Memory & Context
description: How OpenClaw remembers useful context and how to improve it
content: AdvancedMemory & ContextHow OpenClaw remembers useful context and how to improve itMemory helps your OpenClaw bot stay useful across conversations. A normal chatbot forgets most things after the chat ends. OpenClaw can keep important context in plain Markdown files, so your assistant can remember preferences, decisions, project details, and working notes. Why Memory Matters Good memory makes your assistant better because it can: remember who you are and how you work keep track of project decisions avoid asking the same questions again continue work across sessions follow your preferred style and rules use past context when helping with new tasks Without memory, every conversation starts from zero. How OpenClaw Stores Memory OpenClaw memory is file-based. The most common files are: 🧠MEMORY.mdLong-term memory for durable facts, preferences, and decisions.📝memory/YYYY-MM-DD.mdDaily notes for recent work, raw context, and session history.📋AGENTS.mdOperating rules and instructions for how the assistant should work.✨SOUL.mdTone, personality, boundaries, and response style. These files live in the OpenClaw workspace and can be updated over time. Memory vs Context Memory and context are related, but not the same. Memory is saved information that should last. Context is the information available during the current task. For example, your preferred timezone belongs in memory. A file you uploaded for one task is current context. How to Improve Memory You can improve memory by being clear about what should be saved. Good examples: Remember that I prefer short answers with clear next actions. Remember that Ampere docs should stay simple and customer-facing. Remember this project decision: pricing names should come from the frontend source file. What to Save Save things that will matter again: names and preferences business goals project rules important decisions repo paths and source-of-truth files lessons learned from mistakes recurring workflows Do not save one-time clutter unless it will help later. Keep Memory Clean Useful memory should be short, accurate, and current. A good rule: daily notes can be messy long-term memory should be curated If something changes, update the memory instead of keeping old facts forever. How Ampere Helps Ampere gives you a managed OpenClaw environment where memory, files, skills, channels, and sessions can work together without you managing the full OpenClaw setup yourself. title: Minimize Token Usage
description: Simple ways to reduce Ampere AI credit usage without technical setup
content: AdvancedMinimize Token UsageSimple ways to reduce Ampere AI credit usage without technical setupToken usage is the amount of text your assistant has to read and write. The more text it reads or writes, the more AI credits you may use. This guide is written for non-technical Ampere users. You do not need to understand models, APIs, or billing internals to use it. The Simple Rule Ampere spends more credits when your assistant has to: read long chats read big files read repeated instructions read large tool results write very long answers use a powerful model for a simple task To reduce usage, give the assistant less noise and ask for shorter, clearer answers. 🎯Be specificAsk for exactly what you need instead of asking the assistant to inspect everything.✂️Keep answers shortTell Ampere the answer length you want: 5 bullets, 10 lines, or one page.🧹Send less clutterShare only the relevant file, message, screenshot, or log section.💡Use the right modelUse cheaper models for simple work and stronger models only for hard work. How Ampere Usage Works Ampere credits are easier to understand than raw AI provider billing: $1 = 1,000 Ampere credits. For normal chat, credits mainly depend on two things: What the assistant reads — your message, previous chat context, files, memory, tool results, and instructions What the assistant writes — the final answer, plan, code, summary, or report Different models have different prices. A powerful model costs more than a smaller model, so model choice matters. BYOK noteIf you use BYOK, your AI provider charges your own key directly. BYOK requests do not use managed Ampere credits. Best Prompts to Save Credits Use these patterns when you want lower usage. Ask for a short answer Give me the answer in 5 bullets. Do not repeat the background. Give me only the next action and the reason. Keep this under 150 words. Ask for a focused answer Only check the pricing section and tell me what is wrong. Look at this error and suggest the most likely fix. Do not review the whole project. Compare only these two options and recommend one. Ask for a summary before continuing Summarize this long conversation into decisions, current status, and next steps. Then continue from the summary. This is useful when a task has gone on for many messages. Ask for changes only Tell me only what changed since the last version. Show only the edited text, not the full document. Give me the final copy only. What Not To Do Avoid these habits if you want to save credits. Choosing the Right Model Use a cheaper or balanced model for: short summaries formatting rewriting simple text extracting key points simple customer replies small brainstorms Use a stronger model for: coding debugging legal or security-sensitive review architecture decisions complex research final business-critical copy A good workflow is: Start with a cheaper model for simple exploration. Use a stronger model when the task becomes difficult. Ask for a short summary before switching models. Sharing Files Without Wasting Credits When working with files, send the smallest useful part. Better: Check the introduction and pricing section only. Better: The bug is in the checkout flow. Inspect only the checkout files first. Better: Here are the 30 lines around the error. Avoid: Read the whole repo and find issues. Here is a full 10,000-line log. I pasted the full document again so you remember it. Keeping Long Projects Cheap Long projects can become expensive because every turn may bring old context forward. Use this process: Start with a short goal. Share only the relevant context. Ask for a small plan. Work one step at a time. After a few steps, ask for a compact summary. Continue from the summary, not the full messy chat. Useful prompt: Before continuing, compress this task into: goal, decisions, files, blockers, and next action. Keep only what is needed. Using Memory the Right Way Memory helps save repeated explanation. Good things to remember: your preferred answer style your company/product context stable project rules naming preferences repeated workflows important decisions Examples: Remember: for Ampere docs, keep writing simple and customer-facing. Remember: when I ask for research, give practical business takeaways first. Do not save temporary clutter. Memory should stay clean. For Teams If your team uses Ampere, agree on simple rules: default to short answers ask for summaries during long threads do not paste full logs unless needed save repeated company context in memory or docs use premium models only for premium work ask for “final answer only” when you do not need reasoning This keeps usage lower and makes answers easier to read. Quick Checklist Before sending a message, ask yourself: Can I ask this in fewer words? Can I give only the relevant file section? Do I need a long answer, or just the next step? Is this simple enough for a cheaper model? Have I repeated instructions that should be saved once? Is this long chat ready for a summary? Examples Expensive prompt Read everything from our old chat, all these logs, the full document, and give a detailed explanation of every possible issue. Better prompt Check only the checkout error below. Give me the top 2 likely causes and the next action. Expensive prompt Rewrite this whole page and explain every change. Better prompt Rewrite this page for non-technical customers. Return only the final copy. Expensive prompt Use the strongest model and deeply analyze this simple caption. Better prompt Make this caption clearer in 3 options. Keep each under 12 words. What We Learned From Research We reviewed current AI provider docs plus Reddit and X discussions about high AI-agent costs. The same advice appeared repeatedly: the biggest waste is usually too much unnecessary context long tool outputs and full logs can drain usage quickly smaller models should handle simple tasks stronger models should be saved for hard decisions long conversations should be summarized before continuing focused workflows beat “read everything” workflows shorter answers often improve both cost and clarity The practical takeaway for Ampere users is simple: give the assistant the right context, not all context.Memory & ContextHow OpenClaw remembers useful context and how to improve itMedia GenerationChoose image generation and image edit defaults

title: Browser Automation
description: Use the Ampere Desktop app for advanced web interaction
content: AutomationBrowser AutomationUse the Ampere Desktop app for advanced web interactionBrowser Automation is an advanced Ampere feature for website interaction. It is different from web search. Web search finds information. Browser automation can work through website flows when a normal search is not enough. What it is for Use Browser Automation for tasks like: opening websites checking what is on a page moving through web flows collecting information from pages that need interaction running workflows that benefit from your desktop network path Do not use it for simple questions that normal chat or web search can answer. What you need Before using it, know these limits: it depends on the Ampere Desktop app the desktop app must be running during browser tasks the feature is marked Alpha in the product plan eligibility can matter setup may take time because Ampere installs required support How to enable it Open Browser AutomationGo to the feature area in the dashboard.Enable the featureIf your plan supports it, start the enable flow.Wait for installAmpere may show an installing state while setup completes.Download the desktop appUse the dashboard download flow if prompted.Keep the app runningBrowser tasks need the desktop app active during use. Desktop app availability The current product download flow shows: macOS available Linux available Windows coming soon Check the dashboard for the latest state. Why the Desktop App Matters Browser Automation runs through the Ampere Desktop app so your bot can interact with websites more like a real browser session. The desktop app helps with: using your own computer and network path keeping browser sessions available during tasks supporting websites that need normal browser behavior handling flows that are harder from a server-only environment Keep the desktop app open when you want Browser Automation to work. Best first test After setup, try one simple browser task before a complex workflow. Example: “Open this page and tell me the main heading and pricing options you see.” This helps separate setup problems from task complexity. content: AutomationScheduled Jobs & AutomationsCreate recurring assistant work in AmpereScheduled Jobs let your OpenClaw bot run work later or on a repeating schedule. Use them for reminders, reports, check-ins, and other tasks you do not want to repeat manually. What Scheduled Jobs are Scheduled Jobs are recurring assistant tasks. They are good for work that should happen: later every day every week every few hours on a clear timetable ⏰Scheduled JobsRecurring assistant tasks.🔍Web SearchFinding information.🌐Browser AutomationInteracting with websites. Separate advanced feature. Good jobs to create Good examples: “Remind me every weekday at 7:30 AM to review my priorities.” “Send me a morning briefing every day at 8 AM.” “Every Friday, prepare a weekly summary of what I finished.” “Check this site regularly and alert me if it goes down.” “Every evening, remind me to close out open tasks.” If the task sounds like “do this every day/week/hour,” it is probably a good Scheduled Job. Best creation flow Describe the job in chatAsk the bot to create the recurring task in plain language.Review it in the dashboardOpen Scheduled Jobs and check that the job exists.Use Run NowTest the job immediately before trusting it long term.Leave it enabledIf the result is good, let it keep running. What you can do from the Scheduled Jobs page The dashboard lets you: see existing jobs check whether a job is enabled pause or resume jobs run a job immediately start from templates like Morning Briefing, Bill Reminder, Price Drop Alert, and Server Down Alert Why Run Now matters Use Run Now to test important jobs. It helps you confirm: the prompt is clear the output is useful the job still works the timing is not the only problem Timezone and credits Timezone matters. If your timezone is wrong, a valid job can run at the wrong local time. Credits and plan state can also matter because Scheduled Jobs are real assistant runs, not simple timer popups. title: Channels
description: Connect your OpenClaw bot to Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and more
content: Core FeaturesChannelsConnect your OpenClaw bot to Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and moreChannels let you use the same hosted OpenClaw bot outside the dashboard. The dashboard stays your main control center. Channels are extra ways to reach the same assistant from apps you already use. Channels shown in Ampere The current dashboard shows these configurable channels: TelegramUses a bot token from @BotFather.DiscordUses a Discord bot token.WhatsAppUses WhatsApp credentials and a QR-based flow.LINEShown with its own setup dialog. The dashboard also lists more channels as coming soon, including Slack, Signal, iMessage, Google Chat, Microsoft Teams, Mattermost, Matrix, IRC, Feishu / Lark, Twitch, Nextcloud Talk, Nostr, Zalo, and WebChat. Telegram Telegram is usually the easiest first channel. You need: a Telegram bot token from @BotFather Basic flow: create a bot with @BotFather copy the token paste it into Channels > Telegram verify and save test the bot in a private DM first See the Telegram guide for groups, topics, privacy mode, and pairing. Discord Discord is useful for server and team workflows. You need: a Discord bot token Message Content Intent enabled in the Discord Developer Portal A valid Discord token can still fail if Message Content Intent is not enabled. WhatsApp WhatsApp uses a more specific setup flow. You may need: Phone number ID Access token QR-based connection steps in the dashboard Partial credentials are not enough. Follow the dashboard prompts closely. LINE LINE is listed in the current dashboard with its own setup dialog. Use the fields shown in the dashboard as the source of truth. Troubleshooting When a channel does not work, check in this order: dashboard channel status token or credential value required provider settings, such as Discord Message Content Intent whether the channel save completed whether the gateway had time to restart Chat & InterfacesUse your OpenClaw bot from the dashboard and connected channelsTelegramUse your OpenClaw assistant from Telegram DMs, groups, and forum topics

Main places to chat 💻Dashboard ChatBest for setup, files, history, models, and full control.💬Connected ChannelsUse Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and more for quick access.🕰️Saved SessionsContinue older work without mixing topics.🎙️Voice-to-TextSpeak a message and send it as text. Good examples: “Summarize this document.” “Review this screenshot and tell me what is wrong.” “Explain this code file.” “Turn this rough note into a clean message.” Saved sessions Ampere saves conversations so you can return to them later. title: Skills
description: Add reusable workflows to your OpenClaw bot
content: Core FeaturesSkillsAdd reusable workflows to your OpenClaw botSkills are reusable workflows for your OpenClaw bot. A skill teaches your bot how to do a specific type of work, such as research, code review, scraping, reporting, support, or media generation. Use a skill when you want the same workflow to work well again and again without writing a long prompt every time. What a Skill Can Include A skill can contain: instructions for the assistant workflow steps reference files templates tool guidance code or scripts when needed Think of a skill like a reusable playbook. It tells your bot how to handle one job properly. Why Use Skills? 🔁Repeatable workTurn a task you do often into a reusable workflow.🎯Better resultsGive the bot clear steps instead of relying on a one-line prompt.🛠️Tool-specific helpTeach the bot how to use a tool, API, website, or file format correctly.📈Business processesBuild workflows for reports, research, support, content, operations, and more. Where to Find Skills Open Dashboard > Skills. From there, you can: browse available skills search skills view installed skills open skill details install free skills purchase paid skills when available create or submit custom skills How to Use a Skill Find a skillOpen the Skills page and search for the workflow you need.Check the detailsRead what the skill does, what setup it needs, and whether it is free or paid.Install itInstall the skill and complete any required setup, such as API keys or credentials.Use it in chatOpen dashboard chat and ask your bot to use the skill for a real task. Example prompts: Use the GitHub skill to review this pull request. Use the research skill to compare these three tools and give me a short recommendation. Use the report skill to turn these notes into a weekly update. Installed skills may also appear in the chat composer when skill mentions are available. Good First Skills Start with skills that solve real repeated work. Good examples: GitHub review workflow web research workflow customer support response workflow weekly report workflow browser automation workflow data cleanup workflow Avoid installing many skills at once. Install one useful skill, test it, then add more. Free, Paid, and Owned Skills Ampere supports different skill states: Free — install and use when available Paid — purchase before use If a skill needs external services, it may ask for setup before it can work. When Setup Is Required Some skills need extra values, such as: API keys environment variables service credentials account IDs project settings This is normal. A skill that connects to another service needs permission and configuration before it can help. Custom Skills If the marketplace does not have the workflow you need, you can create a custom skill. Custom skills are useful for: your company process your reporting format your research method your support style your internal tools your preferred templates A good custom skill should be clear and narrow. “Create weekly client reports” is better than “help with marketing.” Common Questions TelegramUse your OpenClaw assistant from Telegram DMs, groups, and forum topicsScheduled Jobs & AutomationsCreate recurring assistant work in Ampere

title: Telegram
description: Use your OpenClaw assistant from Telegram DMs, groups, and forum topics
content: Core FeaturesTelegramUse your OpenClaw assistant from Telegram DMs, groups, and forum topicsTelegram is one of the most useful channels for OpenClaw because it works on phone, desktop, and browser. In Ampere, Telegram is an access point for the same hosted OpenClaw bot you use in the dashboard. It is not a separate assistant. Quick setup Create a bot with BotFatherOpen Telegram, search for @BotFather, and send /newbot.Copy the tokenBotFather gives you a token. Treat it like a password.Connect in AmpereOpen Dashboard > Channels > Telegram, paste the token, verify it, and save.Test in private DMOpen your Telegram bot and send /start or a simple real message.Approve pairing if neededIf your OpenClaw bot asks for pairing approval, complete that flow.Add groups laterOnly add the bot to groups after private DM works. Where Telegram fits 📱Private DMBest for personal assistant use, quick tasks, files, and reminders.👥GroupBest when a team or project room needs to call the assistant in.🧵Forum topicBest for separate work lanes inside one Telegram group. Private DMs Use DMs for: personal questions reminders summaries quick follow-ups file forwarding testing the bot before group use OpenClaw often uses pairing or allowlists for DMs. This protects your assistant from unknown people who find the bot. Groups Groups are useful for shared work, but they need cleaner rules. In most groups, the bot should respond only when: mentioned replied to explicitly allowed by group settings This keeps the bot helpful without interrupting every conversation. Forum topics Telegram forum topics are separate lanes inside one group. They are useful for: research ops alerts planning files code review recurring job output Topics help keep one group from becoming one messy assistant thread. Files, images, and voice notes Telegram can send useful context to your OpenClaw bot: screenshots PDFs and documents CSV or text files voice notes photos forwarded messages links For larger file work, use the Workspace. Telegram is best for fast capture and quick review. BotFather settings worth checking After creating the bot, you can improve the Telegram experience with: /setdescription /setabouttext /setuserpic /setcommands /setjoingroups /setprivacy For most Ampere users, only the token is required. These settings just make the bot easier to understand and manage. Protect your tokenDo not paste your Telegram bot token into public chats, screenshots, or support threads. If it leaks, rotate it in BotFather and update Ampere. Privacy mode and groups Telegram bots do not always see every group message. This depends on Telegram privacy mode, admin status, and your OpenClaw/Ampere configuration. Use this rule: keep privacy mode on for normal mention-based group behavior disable privacy mode or make the bot an admin only when the bot truly needs to see more messages Troubleshooting Check these first: token copied correctly from BotFather channel verified and saved in Ampere gateway had time to restart private DM works before group testing pairing or allowlist is approved group privacy mode matches the behavior you expect forum topic is the right one if using topics ChannelsConnect your OpenClaw bot to Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and moreSkillsAdd reusable workflows to your OpenClaw bot

title: Credits & Pricing
description: Understand Ampere credits, plans, BYOK, and top-ups
content: Credits & PricingUnderstand Ampere credits, plans, BYOK, and top-upsAmpere uses credits for managed AI usage. The core rule is simple: $1 = 1,000 Ampere credits. Credits are used for chat models and media generation. Different models cost different amounts because provider prices are different. How credits work 💬Chat modelsCharged from input and output token usage.🖼️Media modelsCharged as a fixed cost per image request. If you use BYOK, model usage goes through your own provider key. BYOK requests do not use Ampere credits. Managed AI plans Current managed plans from the Ampere frontend config: Free — $0/mo, 5,000 credits, 2 vCPU, 2GB RAM, 20GB storage Pro — $39/mo, 20,000 credits, 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM, 40GB storage Ultra — $79/mo, 40,000 credits, 8 vCPU, 16GB RAM, 80GB storage Unlimited — $299/mo, 40,000 credits plus unlimited Claude model credits, 12 vCPU, 24GB RAM, 120GB storage Business — $499/mo, custom credits, 16 vCPU, 32GB RAM, 200GB storage Plan features can include hosting, web search, cloud backup, auto update, BYOK support, auto top-up, browser automation, and priority support depending on the plan. BYOK plans BYOK means “bring your own key.” Ampere hosts OpenClaw, but model billing goes through your provider account. Current BYOK plan options in the frontend config: BYOK Starter — $9.99/mo, 4 vCPU, 4GB RAM, 40GB storage BYOK Pro — $19.99/mo, 6 vCPU, 8GB RAM, 80GB storage BYOK Ultra — $39.99/mo, 8 vCPU, 16GB RAM, 120GB storage BYOK Max — $59.99/mo, 12 vCPU, 24GB RAM, 200GB storage BYOK Enterprise — $89.99/mo, 16 vCPU, 30GB RAM, 300GB storage Team plans Team plans are priced per seat and support shared usage. Managed team plans: Team Pro — $39/seat, 20,000 credits, 4 vCPU, 8GB RAM, 40GB storage Team Ultra — $79/seat, 40,000 credits, 8 vCPU, 16GB RAM, 80GB storage Team Unlimited — $299/seat, 40,000 credits plus unlimited Claude model credits, 12 vCPU, 24GB RAM, 120GB storage Team BYOK plans use the same BYOK tiers as individual BYOK plans. Media generation credits Media models use fixed credit costs per request: Seedream 4.5 — 50 standard, 50 HD GPT Image 1.5 — 43 standard, 166 HD Flux 2 Flex — 63 standard, 125 HD Nano Banana 2 — 100 standard, 150 HD Nano Banana Pro — 188 standard, 281 HD Simple media tipUse Standard while testing ideas. Use HD when you need a polished final result. Choosing a model Use cheaper models for simple tasks and premium models for important work. For everyday chat, use a budget or balanced model. For coding, analysis, or careful writing, use a stronger model. For image work, test in Standard before spending HD credits. If you are unsure, use Ampere Auto and review the result. Common questions Getting StartedStart using Ampere well after your OpenClaw bot is readyChat & InterfacesUse your OpenClaw bot from the dashboard and connected channels

title: Getting Started
description: Start using Ampere well after your OpenClaw bot is ready
content: Getting StartedStart using Ampere well after your OpenClaw bot is readyThis guide helps you start using Ampere in a useful way. OpenClaw is powerful, but self-hosting it means dealing with Node versions, install commands, provider keys, gateway setup, channel config, daemon/service setup, health checks, and config validation. Ampere handles that hard setup so you can start from the dashboard.
